title: The absolute Galois group of a finite field
statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and $K^{\rm sep}$ a separable
closure. For every $n\geq1$ there is exactly one subextension
$K\subseteq K_n\subseteq K^{\rm sep}$ of degree $n$, namely the set of roots of
$T^{q^n}-T$; it is Galois over $K$ with cyclic group of order $n$ generated by the
Frobenius $\phi(x)=x^q$. Consequently
$\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\rm sep}/K)\cong\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/n=\widehat{\mathbf Z}$
as profinite groups, with $\phi$ corresponding to $1$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements], write $q=p^a$ with $p$ prime and $a\geq1$; in particular $q\geq2$. By [lem-sfb-finite-field-separable-closure-algebraic], the given $K^{\rm sep}$ is an algebraic closure of $K$. Apply [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure] with $k_0=K$, $k=K^{\rm sep}$ and the given embedding. For each $n\geq1$ this constructs the subfield $K_n=\{x:x^{q^n}=x\}$ containing $K$, proves $|K_n|=q^n$, and proves uniqueness among subfields with that cardinality. This establishes existence, which the imported argument starting with an already given degree-$n$ extension did not establish.

source.place: Paragraph 1, first four sentences; supply the missing existence argument using the existing unique-subfield lemma.

proof.text: For any finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $V$ of dimension $s$, choose a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. The map $K^s\to V$, $(c_i)\mapsto\sum_i c_i b_i$, is bijective: spanning gives existence and linear independence gives uniqueness of coefficients. Thus $|V|=q^s$. The finite set $K_n$ spans itself over $K$, so it is finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. To obtain a basis, successively delete a vector expressible in terms of the remaining vectors; this terminates, keeps the same span, and leaves a linearly independent set, since a nonzero coefficient in a linear relation would express one remaining vector in terms of the others. Writing $s=[K_n:K]$, the formula gives $q^s=q^n$, hence $s=n$ since $q\geq2$. Conversely any degree-$n$ intermediate field $E$ has $q^n$ elements by the same coordinate bijection; uniqueness from step 1 gives $E=K_n$.

source.place: Paragraph 1, first sentence and uniqueness: the elementary basis-coordinate count relating degree to cardinality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius] to $K\subseteq K_n$, both finite fields, using $[K_n:K]=n$ from step 2. It gives that $K_n/K$ is Galois, that $\phi_n:x\mapsto x^q$ has order $n$, and that its first $n$ powers are exactly its automorphisms. Therefore $\operatorname{Gal}(K_n/K)$ is cyclic of order $n$. The map $\theta_n:\mathbf Z/n\to\operatorname{Gal}(K_n/K)$, $[j]\mapsto\phi_n^j$, is well defined since $\phi_n^n=1$, multiplicative since powers add, and bijective by the stated power bijection. In particular $\theta_n(1)=\phi_n$.

source.place: Paragraph 1, Galois and cyclic-generator conclusions. The cited Mathlib leaf proves the same smaller-order root-count argument (Finite/Basic.lean:374-394).

proof.text: Let phi be the arithmetic Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-substitution]. Its powers are dense in Gal(Ks/K). Indeed, let H be their closed subgroup closure. Every H-fixed element is fixed by phi, hence lies in K by FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic_apply_eq_self_iff (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finite.Basic). Thus the fixed field of H is K. InfiniteGalois.fixingSubgroup_fixedField (Mathlib.FieldTheory.Galois.Infinite:146) gives H=Gal(Ks/K). The extension is Galois by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois]. Its Galois group is compact by the profinite Krull-limit identification [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit], as supplied by the Mathlib CompactSpace instance.

source.place: Paragraph 2: Frobenius and the inverse limit; density proved with Mathlib infinite Galois correspondence and the existing fixed-Frobenius lemma.

proof.text: For each finite-index normal subgroup H of multiplicative Z, put Q=Z/H and let g be the image of 1. Q is finite, so n=orderOf(g)>0, including n=1 for the trivial quotient. Take the degree-n root field Kn from steps 1-3. Restriction Gal(Ks/K) -> Gal(Kn/K) is continuous by InfiniteGalois.restrictNormalHom_continuous. Follow it with monoidHomOfForallMemZpowers, sending the generating Frobenius phi_n to g, whose order is n. This last map is continuous since the finite Galois group is discrete. Restriction sends phi to phi_n by its power formula and AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom_apply. The resulting continuous homomorphism f_H therefore sends phi to the image of 1.

source.place: Paragraph 2: finite cyclic quotients and their Frobenius generators; direct construction for every quotient of Z.

proof.text: Two continuous homomorphisms out of Gal(Ks/K) agreeing on phi agree on all its integer powers and hence everywhere by density. Consequently the maps f_H are compatible under quotient transition maps. The tuple F(x)=(f_H(x))_H is a continuous homomorphism to ProfiniteCompletion.completion(Multiplicative Z), with F(phi)=etaFn(1). Its image contains etaFn(Z), which is dense by ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion.denseRange. Compactness of the source makes the image closed, proving surjectivity. To prove injectivity, take an open normal subgroup U of the Galois group P and its finite quotient pi:P -> P/U. Set H=ker(pi composed with the Frobenius-power homomorphism Z -> P); this has finite index. QuotientGroup.lift factors that composite through Z/H. The continuous maps pi and this factor composed with f_H agree at phi, hence everywhere. If F(x)=1, its H coordinate gives pi(x)=1. This holds for every U, so ProfiniteGrp.toLimit_injective gives x=1. The continuous bijection F between compact Hausdorff spaces is a homeomorphism by Continuous.homeoOfEquivCompactToT2; its multiplicativity and value on phi are already established. This uses the compatible-quotient construction directly without classifying subgroups of Z or reindexing an inverse limit.

source.place: Paragraph 2: compatible tuples, topology, and Frobenius corresponds to 1; fully proved coordinatewise in completion_equiv.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs 1-2; S7 Lean proof retains the finite root fields and cyclic quotients, and constructs the completion coordinates directly. Density uses the proved Frobenius fixed-element lemma and Mathlib infinite Galois correspondence; compactness uses the existing Krull-limit theorem.

lean.statement: theorem finiteField_absoluteGaloisGroup (K : Type u) (Ks : Type v) [Field K] [Field Ks] [Fintype K] [Algebra K Ks] [IsSepClosure K Ks] : ∃ φ : Gal(Ks / K), (∀ x : Ks, φ x = x ^ Fintype.card K) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ Kn : IntermediateField K Ks, Module.finrank K Kn = n ∧ (∀ E : IntermediateField K Ks, Module.finrank K E = n → E = Kn) ∧ (∀ x : Ks, x ∈ Kn ↔ Polynomial.eval₂ (algebraMap K Ks) x (Polynomial.X ^ (Fintype.card K ^ n) - Polynomial.X) = 0) ∧ IsGalois K Kn ∧ ∃ φn : Kn ≃ₐ[K] Kn, (∀ x : Kn, φn x = x ^ Fintype.card K) ∧ orderOf φn = n ∧ (∀ g : Kn ≃ₐ[K] Kn, ∃ j : ZMod n, g = φn ^ j.val)) ∧ ∃ e : Gal(Ks / K) ≃ₜ* ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion.completion (GrpCat.of (Multiplicative ℤ)), e φ = ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion.etaFn (GrpCat.of (Multiplicative ℤ)) (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ))
